svg.text: The dashboard, traced — how a published number comes out wrong
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which is the whole subject of ch01:
3 // et = event time, when the thing happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed (clicks, here) · key = which stream it belongs to
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late one
9 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
10 // primitive: MIN — seconds in a dashboard minute. MIN = 60
11 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
12 // primitive: minOf(sec) — the START of the MIN-second minute holding sec.
14 // primitive: add(m, k, n) — add n to m[k], starting from 0 when k is absent.
16 // primitive: keysOf(m) — m's keys, ascending. keysOf({0: 12, 60: 7}) = [0, 60]
20 // primitive: M0 — the dashboard minute this trace follows. M0 = 0 (12:00)
21 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — the completeness claim after event i:
22 // the highest event time seen through i, minus LAG.
25 // function: onEvent(dash, e, i) — the whole dashboard, per arriving event.
36 // function: publishDue(dash, i) — declare every minute the watermark has passed.
46 // function: onLate(dash, e, policy) — the three options, as one branch each.
49 // onLate(dash, EVENTS[7], "wait") never reached: nothing was published yet
56 // function: main() — THE CALLER: replay the stream into the dashboard.
Step 1/0 — the 12:00 minute accumulates the events that have arrived
After events 0 and 1, `display[0]` holds 5 + 3 = 8. `closed` is false — the minute has not been published, so nothing is a revision yet. Everything here is
correct; the problem is not in this function.
